theorem_title: The fixed two-state suffix algebra satisfies every YAH rule equation
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be the list of all eleven YAH rules and let $A_s$ denote the specified Boolean unary map of a symbol $s$. For a word $s_1\cdots s_k$, define $E(s_1\cdots s_k,b)=A_{s_1}(\cdots A_{s_k}(b)\cdots)$, with $E(\varnothing,b)=b$. Then

$$\forall r\in\mathcal R\;\forall b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\},\qquad E(\operatorname{lhs}(r),b)=E(\operatorname{rhs}(r),b).$$

This verifies the rule equations for the one fixed two-state algebra used for suffix labeling. It does not assert that any induced order proves termination.
preamble:

theorem CollatzWork.YAH.twoState_rule_equations :

      evalWord (rule name).lhs tail = evalWord (rule name).rhs tail := by sorry
